# PR #160 phase 2 correctness review

## A) Verdict

**BLOCK** at `f886b8f13f52a6fbc5a75bfb360ba8a97bc1a0d9`.

F001: shrink-only exemptions are not enforced. F002: directory-read failures can produce a false coverage pass. F003: the live procedure still prints deleted roadmap addresses.

## B) Scope and evidence

Reviewed phase 2 against merged phase 1 `59120b3`, including rename, sensor, integration, templates, states and the deferred governance helper. Clean pinned checkout; GitHub and ls-remote agree, CLEAN, latest Delivers SUCCESS.

CI `42393669106`, attempt 1, matches this head: both Node versions ran all five coverage tests and report 2,209 passed/six skipped overall; Rust JUnit has 2,122 cases, zero failures/errors. Pin/embedding and dual-folder reader/claim controls executed.

The findings below are source-derived, not local fault reproductions. No local product builds/tests, sensor execution, mutations, live governance edits or cost probes were run.

## C) F001, P2: a new real gap plus its exemption passes

`coverage-check.ts:98-121` exempts any supplied address that names an existing uncovered row. It rejects nonexistent and now-covered rows, but has no frozen allowed-address set or equivalent restriction to the initial 15 gaps.

Add a new planned requirement and an exemption for that same address with an owner/reason: it enters gaps, exempt.has skips it, and neither stale/unknown check fires. The command returns a coverage pass with an increased exempted count. The repo test only requires that count to be greater than zero, so it passes too.

Therefore "only shrinks" is prose, not a guard. Unknown means nonexistent here, not an unauthorized new exemption. Restrict the repo exemption set to a subset of the accepted 15 addresses, validate its owner/reason metadata, and add a new-real-row-plus-new-exemption negative. Merely capping the count would still permit replacing an old exemption with a new one.

## D) F002, P2: unreadable folders are treated as empty

`readDocs` catches every readdirSync error and returns [] (`coverage-check.ts:141-147`), without distinguishing deliberate legacy-folder absence from an unreadable required input.

For example, if docs/project/blueprints cannot be read because of EACCES/EIO, repoFindings supplies no components to inspect. The current requirement-side gaps are still the accepted 15; all other requirements have steps. The result has no findings and main prints "every requirement and component is covered" with exit 0 despite never seeing the blueprint rows.

Propagate or explicitly report discovery failures. Tolerate only intentionally absent optional/legacy locations, not arbitrary read errors. Add a filesystem-discovery failure control alongside the healthy/absent-legacy positive. The current five cases do not exercise this error boundary.

## E) F003, P2: live examples still point at the removed folder

`skills/pij/references/community/README.md:12` names the full-size example as docs/project/roadmaps/001-pij-community.dd.json. Line 45 still teaches a Delivers address in that deleted file.

The old path is absent; the current workstream is under docs/project/workstreams. These are live instructions, not historical text or the deliberate claim/reader alias. Replace both with the moved address; a PM following the procedure should not copy a nonexistent target.

**N001, P3:** related transitional wording still says "until plan 210 moves" in this README:23, PRD 001 req-18 and blueprint c-doc-schemas. Update those live statements to the completed rename while preserving historical workshops, changelogs and shipped template bytes.

## F) What is correct

- Commit a567520 moves both project/worked-example docs and switches both to pij/workstream together. Existing same-file links remain valid.
- Direct isolated ddocs validation returned zero errors/warnings for the moved workstream/example, PRD and plan/task/backpressure documents; all six regenerated faces match exactly. PM v4 validates at depth 0. This is documentation proof, not CI ddocs proof.
- All 28 previously shipped template files are byte-identical to phase 1; all 29 current hashes match. PM v4 changes the path, version and changelog only.
- The normal new-gap, built-component, dropped-row, stale/unknown-exemption and cross-file umbrella/missing-parent cases are correctly asserted and ran in CI.
- Coverage is a non-advisory, non-heavy harness checks stage and a self-check step. It performs one document sweep per invocation, not one literal filesystem read, with no new recurring loop.
- Existing readers/claims support both folders; their legacy tests are appropriate and must remain.

## G) States and Delivers

The three Delivers addresses exist: workstream s16 and req-30/req-31. s16 links both requirements and the existing schema component and names plan 210. req-24/req-27 provenance additions match the read-only deliveries ledger: #141/#159 and #136/#159 respectively.

The umbrella control supports req-30's roll-up, but the coverage finality claim for req-31/AC6/s16 must not hide F001/F002. Fix before relying on their checked/shipped/complete labels.

AC4's known gaps and AC7's merge-time edits remain explicitly deferred; AC7 is unchecked and its evidence is a dry run, not eight committed edits. No live edits were performed by this reviewer. F104 accurately discloses CI's ddocs UNAVAILABLE limitation; it does not excuse the sensor's separate I/O false-pass path. No migration changed.

## H) Handover

Freeze a repair with new-gap-plus-exemption and discovery-failure controls, and correct the live addresses. Preserve the shrink-compatible legacy set, umbrella positives, pinned versions and same-commit schema move. Harness observation DL-009 records the missing proof. No product code was changed by this reviewer.
